status: Native layer labels, selected visibility and Option-eye restoration tested; live qualification pending
implementation: Atomic selected label changes preserve layer content, selection, unrelated tags and reserved lclr bytes; no-op labels do not create undo entries.
Row context exposes all existing label choices with mixed-state validation; unselected-row context changes target only that row.
Selected Hide/Show Layers binds the existing factory Command-comma entry and appears in contextual Layers menus.

Eye-column hidden state uses blank space; Option-click isolates/restores without changing selection; source-derived maps retain descendant flags and reveal ancestor paths. Already-solo layouts with no snapshot reveal all rows; ancestor-alias restoration retains the saved snapshot.
Isolation snapshots belong to each document, survive unrelated edits and unrelated Undo, and retire after visibility/topology changes or document read/close.
Snapshot diagnostics freeze the final model after all fixture edits, preventing setup from restarting asynchronous rendering during capture.
limits: Actual native pointer/menu/keyboard and Photoshop appearance require an unlocked Mac; callback/offscreen tests do not qualify physical interaction.

Exact color-menu order/swatches, locked/group label inheritance, mixed-selection Show/Hide policy, group/clipping rendering, topology invalidation and history behavior remain unqualified against Photoshop.
Eye-column dragging, recursive disclosure, Panel Options and confirmation preferences remain incomplete.
Native/PSD label round trips and rendering invariance are bounded regression evidence, not Photoshop-wide byte equivalence.
Earlier step077 pixel/History text capture variation and Desktop FinderInfo signature instability remain tracked; clean ZIP is the qualified distribution artifact.
Full Photoshop2026 feature/byte equality and macOS14/Intel runtime certification remain incomplete.
